---
title: "From health records to published statistics"
description: "A plain-language overview of the BNR statistical production pathway."
---

BNR statistics are produced through a controlled sequence. Health information is assessed and prepared before any aggregate result is approved for publication.

## The statistical journey

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  A["Health records and notifications"] --> B["Eligible events identified"]
  B --> C["Records checked and prepared"]
  C --> D["Aggregate statistics calculated"]
  D --> E["Quality, confidentiality and approval checks"]
  E --> F["Published BNR outputs"]
```

## What happens at each stage

| Stage | Public explanation |
|---|---|
| **Identify** | Potentially eligible events or records are found from approved sources. |
| **Classify** | Registry definitions are applied so that comparable events are grouped consistently. |
| **Prepare** | Duplicates, dates, residence, missing values and logical inconsistencies are checked. |
| **Calculate** | Stated numerators, denominators and statistical methods are applied. |
| **Review** | Results, supporting metadata and confidentiality checks are reviewed before approval. |
| **Publish** | Only approved aggregate products enter the public Info-Hub. |

## Why published values can change

Registry information can mature after an initial release. A late record may arrive, an uncertain outcome may be resolved, or a source error may be corrected. BNR therefore identifies release periods and explains material revisions.

The aim is not to prevent correction. It is to make corrections controlled, documented and understandable.

## What to remember

- Publication is separate from calculation.
- Public figures are aggregates, not identifiable patient records.
- Definitions and coverage matter as much as the displayed number.
- A revised value is not necessarily evidence of an error in the original analysis; it may reflect more complete information.
